name: Domaine Auguste Clape Cornas 2013
text:
## Domaine Auguste Clape Cornas 2013

**The story.** Clape is the legend of Cornas. Thatcher's Wine compares Auguste Clape to Henri Gouges in Burgundy: in 1957 he became the first producer in [Cornas](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Domaine+Clape,+Cornas,+France&t=k) to bottle his own wine. His son Pierre-Marie worked beside him from 1989 and is now joined by his own son, Olivier; Auguste died in 2018 at 93, and "there are no plans to change the style or methods", Thatcher's says: "this house is a beacon of traditional excellence" ([Thatcher's Wine](https://www.thatcherswine.com/products/2013-auguste-clape-cornas)).

**The wine.** Where many producers now bottle single vineyards, Clape still blends an array of plots, including Chaillot, Reynard, La Côte and Sabarotte, the last inherited from the late Noël Verset, some with vines over a century old and very low-yielding. The reds never see new oak: they are fermented as whole bunches, almost no press wine is used, and they age in old foudres. Younger vines (still 20 to 25 years old) go into a second Cornas, Renaissance ([Thatcher's Wine](https://www.thatcherswine.com/products/2013-auguste-clape-cornas)). For the 2013, the Wine Advocate reports 100% [Syrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah), no destemming and 22 months in mostly ancient foudres.

**About Cornas.** [Cornas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornas_AOC) is one of the smallest appellations in the Rhône, and makes only red wine, entirely from [Syrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah). Its steep east-south-east-facing slopes, between 100 and 400 metres, lie just north of [Valence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valence,_Dr%C3%B4me), south of [Tain-l'Hermitage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tain-l'Hermitage). Sheltered from the cold [mistral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mistral_%28wind%29), it is often the first northern Rhône appellation to begin harvesting ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornas_AOC)).

**From the history books**
- **"Burnt earth."** The name Cornas is said to be Celtic for "burnt earth", and wine is mentioned here as early as 885. [Louis XV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XV) and [Cardinal Richelieu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Richelieu) are said to have admired it ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornas_AOC)).
- **Bottling at home.** Cornas became an appellation in 1938, but local growers only began bottling their own wine around 1950 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornas_AOC)). Pierre-Auguste Clape, who began estate-bottling in the 1950s, died in 2018 aged 93; Alain Voge, born in 1939, was another of the small group that built Cornas's international reputation ([Decanter](https://www.decanter.com/obituaries/alain-voge-dies-cornas-rhone-443632/)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [northern Rhône vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/northern-rhone) calls 2013 "very promising reds which may well have excellent longevity". Despite a slow start and mildew in June, warm days and cool nights through the summer turned the season around, and rain prompted a speedy harvest, one of the latest ever; "the best reds could last for decades more".

**What the critics say for 2013.** As listed by [Thatcher's Wine](https://www.thatcherswine.com/products/2013-auguste-clape-cornas):
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 95**. "Probably the wine of the vintage": classic Clape notes of "beef blood, cold steel, liquid rock, pepper and saddle leather (there's fruit in there as well)"; medium to full-bodied, beautifully concentrated and textured, with an awesome mid-palate and ripe tannin. Not as long-lived as the blockbuster years, but "incredible pleasure over the coming 10-15 years".
- **[Vinous](https://vinous.com): 95**. Glass-staining ruby: cassis, boysenberry, incense, smoky bacon and minerals; dense, fresh and energetic, with an alluring sweetness on an extremely persistent, smoky-mineral finish.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 92.5** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is thirteen years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2020 to 2029, and the Wine Advocate's 10 to 15 years from release run to about 2026 to 2031. So it is in its prime now: blood, iron, pepper, smoked meat and dark fruit. Drink it over the next few years; decant an hour ahead.

**Serving and food.** Serve at 16 to 17°C. Cornas loves grilled and roast meat: lamb with rosemary, venison, a peppered steak, duck, or a [cassoulet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassoulet).

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Clape, which is allocated and hard to find; look to fine-wine merchants and auctions.

**Curious details**
- **Inherited vines.** The Sabarotte parcel came from Noël Verset, another of Cornas's great traditional growers ([Thatcher's Wine](https://www.thatcherswine.com/products/2013-auguste-clape-cornas)).
- **A white too.** Clape makes one white, a [Saint-Péray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-P%C3%A9ray_AOC) of 80% Marsanne and 20% Roussanne ([Thatcher's Wine](https://www.thatcherswine.com/products/2013-auguste-clape-cornas)).
